thread.title: The 10 Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018

author: James Brumley
title: The 10 Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018
text:

Breaking news sponsored by Home > Stock Picks > Stocks to Buy > The 10 Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018 Aug 21, 2018, 3:27 pm EDT August 21, 2018 The 10 Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018 We're at the halfway point of the year. Time to reassess and regroup. http://bit.ly/2w3LMoH Source: Shutterstock
We’re halfway through 2018, and all the major market indices are beginning to rumble with breakout potential. Since mid-June, the S&P 500 is up roughly 7%, but only about 4% since the start of the year. But led by double-digit performances by Nike (NYSE: NKE ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) in the Dow Jones , and 80%, 90% and 200% gains from the S&P’s best stocks to buy, the market is on the verge of shedding 2018’s correction.
Still, investors can’t afford to go on autopilot … especially considering most stocks are pushing their valuation limits. Now, more than ever, it pays to be picky.
With that as the backdrop, here’s a rundown of 10 of the best stocks to buy for the latter half of 2018. Some of these stocks earned a spot on the list for technical reasons, while others are fundamental bargains. Still, others are heading for massive growth.
In all 10 cases, though, there’s something outstanding that makes these stocks better than most other names to choose from.
In no certain order …
[ Editor’s note: This story is a replay that was previously published on June 26, 2017. It has since been republished and updated to reflect up-to-date information. ] Source: Rob Schreckhise via Flickr
When investors think of an aerospace and defense stock, companies like Textron (NYSE: TXT ) generally don’t come to mind. With a market cap of only $17 billion, TXT just doesn’t turn many heads.
That doesn’t mean it’s not worth owning. Indeed, here in the middle of 2018, Textron is a hidden gem within the world of defense.
Textron is not only the name behind Bell helicopters, but it’s also the owner of Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft. More relevant in light of a rekindled war on terror and more aggressive regimes though, Textron makes drones (air and sea), armored military vehicles , electronic warfare systems and more.
Much of it is the stuff you don’t think about — and rarely see — but it’s all important in the support of the strong defense initiatives that President Donald Trump seems to want. Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018: Alphabet (GOOGL) Source: Shutterstock
The market’s opinions on internet giant Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL , NASDAQ: GOOG ) may run hot and cold, but a closer look at the company’s historical results reveals the company’s revenue and earnings growth is a picture of consistency.
Alphabet, the parent company of Google, is now into its 12th straight year of revenue growth .
It’s not just annualized revenue growth. In almost every single quarter during that timeframe, year-over-year sales have grown, and for all intents and purposes, quarterly earnings have done the same.
In other words, love it or hate it, Alphabet is a juggernaut. That consistency alone is enough to earn it a spot on a list of stocks to buy for any six-month stretch. Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018: Constellation Brands (STZ) Source: Shutterstock
You may not be familiar with the name Constellation Brands, Inc. (NYSE: STZ ), but odds are good you’re familiar with at least some of the brand names of booze it sells. Constellation owns Corona, Wild Irish Rose, Woodbridge , and other popular beers and spirits.
Its brand names alone make STZ one of a few great stocks to buy for the rest of the year. But it’s not a quality product alone that puts Constellation Brands near the top of a relatively short list of potential purchases.
Alcoholic beverage stocks tend to do well even when the rest of the market is struggling, as beer and liquor are just one of those vices most consumers don’t give up even when times are tough.
It’s mostly a perception thing, but that doesn’t mean the strategy doesn’t pay off. Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018: Garmin (GRMN) Source: Shutterstock
Most investors are a little more familiar with Garmin Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRMN ) is a company most investors are familiar with. It got its start years ago when then-new GPS and satellite-positioning technologies made in-car digital mapping a possibility.
Since then the company’s branched out, wading into wearables and action cameras.
And, surprise! Garmin is actually growing the top and bottom lines. Its results are a little uneven and its growth is anything but red-hot. But GRMN forward P/E is priced at 19, which isn’t bad for a company growing per-share earnings at a 36.5% clip this year.
Bonus: The dividend yield of 3.2% is generous, too. Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018: Cutera (CUTR) Source: Shutterstock
Don’t sweat it if you haven’t heard of Cutera (NASDAQ: CUTR ) — most people haven’t.
Cutera makes cosmetic surgery technology, and while it’s tops in its respective field, that’s not exactly a high-profile arena.
What makes CUTR worthy as one of a few stocks to buy as we enter the back half of 2018 is the sales growth that has materialized just within the past couple of quarters, and the subsequent swing to a profit. Sales were up 26% in the fourth quarter of last year , and the company doubled its earnings.
The first quarter’s numbers weren’t quite as impressive, but still encouraging. Its new enlighten III platform was a key growth driver, and its recently-approved truSculpt technology holds a lot of promise.
It’s small, even by small-cap standards, so be smart about handling it if you wade in. But Cutera could be one of the best stocks to buy over the next year or so, as 2018 could be a real breakout period for CUTR.
Analysts certainly think so. They’ve modeled more than a doubling of the bottom line, and revenue growth of nearly 19%. Best Stocks to Buy for the Rest of 2018: Ulta Beauty (ULTA) Source: Shutterstock
If you’ve ever been in an Ulta Beauty Inc (NASDAQ: ULTA ) beauty supply store, you’ll know why it has earned a spot on a list of stocks to buy for the second half of the year.
It’s usually packed.
There’s rarely a bad time to step into this stunningly reliable growth machine. The evidence: Last year’s top line of $5.8 billion was 21% better than 2016, and the bottom line of $555 million grew 35% year-over-year.
The kicker here is the fact that ULTA shares didn’t have a great month, sliding more than 5% since mid-July. That dip means you don’t have to pay as steep a premium as you did earlier this year to get into this seemingly untouchable, mostly Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN )-proof retail growth story.
